metadata.title: Anti-harassment and complaint procedure
metadata.text:
# Anti-harassment and complaint procedure

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Anti-harassment and complaint procedure
metadata.text:
## 1. Coverage and prohibited conduct
GridAxon prohibits harassment, discrimination, and retaliation in offices, remote work, messaging, client sites, conferences, business travel, and work-related social events. This policy covers employees, applicants, interns, contractors, managers, clients, and vendors. Sexual demands, unwelcome touching, discriminatory slurs, repeated degrading messages, and intimidation can violate policy even when conduct does not meet a legal liability threshold. Protection covers race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, and other legally protected characteristics.

metadata.title: Anti-harassment and complaint procedure
metadata.text:
## 2. Reporting routes
Report to People Operations, the CEO, or the designated independent Board contact. Any route may be used directly; there is no requirement to approach the alleged offender or a supervisor first. If a complaint involves the CEO, use the independent Board contact. If People Operations is involved, use the CEO or Board contact. These are fictional role-based channels, not live inboxes; real contact details must be inserted and tested before adoption.
Reports may be oral or written. Include dates, conduct, witnesses, and relevant messages when available. Missing details or delayed reporting do not prevent review. Anonymous reports are accepted, although anonymity can limit investigation. Managers must forward concerns to an uninvolved reporting contact within one business day.

metadata.title: Anti-harassment and complaint procedure
metadata.text:
## 3. Response and investigation
People Operations targets acknowledgment within two business days and initial safety assessment within one business day. These are internal service targets, not filing deadlines or guarantees. Assign an impartial investigator without a reporting conflict; use an external investigator when necessary. Preserve evidence, interview involved people and witnesses, review records, and document findings. Target completion within 20 business days; provide periodic updates when more time is needed.

metadata.title: Anti-harassment and complaint procedure
metadata.text:
Do not promise absolute confidentiality: share information only as reasonably necessary for review, corrective action, and legal duties.
Interim measures may include reporting-line changes, scheduling adjustments, or access restrictions without presuming guilt or penalizing a complainant. Corrective action can range from training to termination or ending a vendor relationship. Communicate completion and appropriate outcome information while respecting privacy. A reporting person may request review by an uninvolved Board contact.

metadata.title: Anti-harassment and complaint procedure
metadata.text:
## 4. Retaliation and external rights
Retaliation for raising a concern, requesting accommodation, participating in an investigation, or otherwise exercising protected rights is prohibited. Report retaliation through any route above. An unsubstantiated report is not itself misconduct. Knowingly fabricated evidence may be addressed separately without punishing good-faith reporting.
Employees may contact the EEOC, TWC Civil Rights Division, law enforcement, or counsel without company permission. Internal review does not pause external filing deadlines. This policy neither guarantees a legal defense nor replaces prevention, training, prompt investigation, and corrective action. See HR-007 for equal opportunity and HR-004 for protected disclosures.

# Offer letter and employment terms template

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Offer letter and employment terms template
metadata.text:
## 1. Offer particulars
Candidate: [full name]. Position: [title]. Start date: [date]. Reporting manager: [name]. Approved work location: [Texas address]. Status: [full-time / part-time]. Wage classification: [exempt / non-exempt, approved through HR-009]. Pay: [annual salary or hourly rate]. Paydays: every other Friday, with required payroll adjustments communicated in advance.

metadata.title: Offer letter and employment terms template
metadata.text:
This template does not make every salaried employee exempt.
Benefits are governed by the current applicable policies and formal benefit-plan documents. No bonus, commission, or equity is promised unless separately described in an authorized written agreement. The sample equity terms in HR-015 do not themselves grant an award. Specify any lawful, job-related contingencies and their completion before the start date; do not use this template as a background-check disclosure or authorization.

metadata.title: Offer letter and employment terms template
metadata.text:
## 2. At-will relationship
Employment is at will. Subject to applicable law, either the employee or GridAxon may end the employment relationship at any time, with or without advance notice and with or without cause. At-will status does not permit unlawful discrimination, retaliation, unpaid earned wages, or interference with protected rights. This letter creates no fixed employment term. Only a written agreement expressly changing at-will status and signed by the CEO and employee may change that status.

metadata.title: Offer letter and employment terms template
metadata.text:
## 3. Other agreements and acceptance
The employee will receive HR-004 confidentiality and IP terms and HR-006 handbook separately. Any restrictive covenant requires its own counsel-approved agreement under HR-005; accepting this offer does not create a non-compete. Entire-agreement wording must preserve separate signed agreements and mandatory legal rights. Amendments to contractual compensation terms require authorized written approval and lawful prospective notice.
Employee signature: __________________ Date: __________
Authorized company signature: __________________ Date: __________
These lines are intentionally blank; no signature or execution is represented. Complete the separate HR-003 acknowledgment during onboarding.

metadata.title: Confidentiality and intellectual property assignment agreement
metadata.text:
# Confidentiality and intellectual property assignment agreement

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Confidentiality and intellectual property assignment agreement
metadata.text:
## 1. Confidential information
Confidential information includes nonpublic client models, interconnection studies, PSS/E and PSCAD cases, source code, pricing, business plans, credentials, and personal data disclosed through work. Use it only for authorized duties; disclose only to authorized recipients; apply HR-013 security controls. Information is excluded if lawfully public without breach, already lawfully known, independently developed without protected information, or lawfully received without a duty of confidence. Protect trade secrets while they remain trade secrets and other confidential information for three years after separation, subject to longer client, privacy, or legal duties.

metadata.title: Confidentiality and intellectual property assignment agreement
metadata.text:
## 2. Assignment and exclusions
For this mock agreement, the employee hereby assigns to GridAxon all rights, title, and interest in work product created within employment duties, specifically commissioned for company work, or developed using company confidential information or resources, to the extent permitted by applicable law. This includes study methods, software, reports, and associated intellectual property. Qualifying works are works made for hire where legally applicable; assignment covers rights not vesting that way.

metadata.title: Confidentiality and intellectual property assignment agreement
metadata.text:
Execute reasonable confirmatory documents at company expense, with reasonable compensation for substantial post-employment assistance.
Schedule A identifies pre-existing inventions and third-party obligations: [list or write none]. Employee retains listed pre-existing material and unrelated personal work developed entirely on personal time without company resources or confidential information and outside assigned duties, subject to applicable law. If approved pre-existing material is embedded in work product, a separate written license must define the company's necessary rights; no third-party rights are silently transferred. Obtain approval before adding open-source components with license obligations.

metadata.title: Confidentiality and intellectual property assignment agreement
metadata.text:
## 3. Protected disclosures
Nothing prohibits lawful reporting to government agencies, communicating with counsel, discussing wages or working conditions as protected by law, or participating in investigations. No prior company notice or permission is required for protected reporting. Under 18 USC 1833(b), an individual is immune from federal and state trade-secret liability for disclosure made in confidence to a government official, directly or indirectly, or an attorney solely to report or investigate a suspected legal violation; or in a complaint or other document filed under seal in a proceeding. In a retaliation lawsuit for reporting a suspected violation, an individual may disclose trade secrets to their attorney and use them in court if filed under seal and not otherwise disclosed except by court order. Other legal protections remain intact.

metadata.title: Confidentiality and intellectual property assignment agreement
metadata.text:
## 4. Return and execution
Return company materials at separation under HR-016, preserving legal holds and protected personal employment records. Do not destroy evidence. This agreement does not promise employment or create a non-compete. Counsel must review assignment boundaries, governing law, client ownership, and any state-specific exclusions before use.
Employee: __________________ Date: __________
Company: __________________ Date: __________
Schedule A: __________________

metadata.text:
# Restrictive covenants review and optional non-solicitation template

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Restrictive covenants review and optional non-solicitation template
metadata.text:
## 1. Default and approval gate
GridAxon's fictional default is no blanket employee non-compete. Confidentiality and IP duties appear in HR-004. Any non-compete or non-solicit must be reviewed individually by Texas employment counsel before presentation. Reasonable time, geography, and activity scope alone do not establish enforceability: Texas law also requires a qualifying connection to an otherwise enforceable agreement, and applicable law and worker circumstances must be checked at execution and enforcement.

metadata.title: Restrictive covenants review and optional non-solicitation template
metadata.section_title: 2. Optional customer non-solicitation terms — NOT ADOPTED
metadata.text:
## 2. Optional customer non-solicitation terms — NOT ADOPTED
For six months after separation, a signatory would refrain from directly soliciting competing energy consulting engagements from covered customers. A covered customer would mean a Texas customer with whom the signatory had material business contact or about whom the signatory received relevant confidential information during the preceding 12 months. The restricted services would be limited to interconnection and transmission-study consulting services the employee materially performed or supervised.

metadata.title: Restrictive covenants review and optional non-solicitation template
metadata.section_title: 2. Optional customer non-solicitation terms — NOT ADOPTED
metadata.text:
Scope would be limited to those covered customer relationships in Texas, rather than every customer or every energy-sector job.
General advertising, unsolicited inbound requests without prohibited solicitation, protected activity, and lawful agency reporting would be excluded. No employee non-solicit or no-hire restriction is created by this sample. This is an illustrative negotiation template; six months or Texas-only scope is not a legal safe harbor. Counsel must determine legitimate interests, consideration, enforceability, potential overbreadth, and effects of other jurisdictions. No agreement exists until a final separate instrument is approved and signed.

metadata.title: Restrictive covenants review and optional non-solicitation template
metadata.text:
## 3. Review record and execution gate
Record employee role, actual confidential access, related enforceable obligations, affected clients, proposed geography and activities, consideration, review date, counsel approval, and employee work jurisdiction. Reassess before enforcement; do not tell employees an unsigned sample binds them. Any remedy or modification requires legal review and applicable court standards.
Draft recipient: __________ Counsel review: __________
Execution status: NOT EXECUTED. Final signature blocks must be added only after approval.

metadata.title: Employee handbook and acknowledgment
metadata.text:
# Employee handbook and acknowledgment

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Employee handbook and acknowledgment
metadata.text:
## 1. Company and scope
GridAxon.io is a fictional energy consulting startup headquartered in Austin, Texas, with 18 employees. It provides grid interconnection, transmission studies, and energy analytics. These invented facts are for the learning dataset, not assertions about an actual legal entity. Policies apply to Texas employees unless a section says otherwise. Contractors receive relevant security and conduct requirements but do not automatically receive employee benefits. Work outside Texas requires HR-011 approval and a local-law review.

metadata.title: Employee handbook and acknowledgment
metadata.text:
## 2. Reading guide and authority
This handbook is a navigation and operating guide. HR-001 governs harassment reporting; HR-007 conduct and equal opportunity; HR-008 leave; HR-009 pay and timekeeping; HR-010 contractor review; HR-011 remote work; HR-012 expenses; HR-013 IT; HR-014 privacy; HR-016 separation. HR-002 through HR-005 and HR-015 contain separate templates or agreements and do not become executed contracts through this handbook.

metadata.title: Employee handbook and acknowledgment
metadata.text: For an ordinary current-policy question use the latest effective, current policy for that topic and the worker's jurisdiction. Archived versions apply only to explicit historical questions about their effective periods. Specific topic policies control over summaries here. Applicable law and valid signed contractual rights control where mandatory or binding; escalate unresolved conflicts to People Operations instead of inventing a rule. No manager may override legal protections or earned compensation through an informal message.

metadata.title: Employee handbook and acknowledgment
metadata.text:
## 3. Employment and administration
Employment remains at will as described in HR-003. The company may revise prospective policies with appropriate notice, subject to law and binding agreements. A progressive disciplinary sequence is not guaranteed. No policy restricts protected reporting, lawful wage discussions, or other protected concerted activity. Request accommodations through People Operations or an uninvolved manager. Personnel records, executed offers, SSNs, and complaint files are access-restricted and excluded from the shared policy index.

metadata.title: Employee handbook and acknowledgment
metadata.text:
## 4. Handbook acknowledgment
I acknowledge receipt of this handbook and access to the topic policies. I understand it is not a fixed-term employment contract, does not waive protected rights, and does not itself execute a restrictive covenant or equity award. I can ask People Operations for clarification or an accessible copy. My signature acknowledges receipt, not consent to unlawful terms.
Employee printed name: __________________
Employee signature: __________________ Date: __________
People Operations receipt: __________________ Date: __________
All signature fields are intentionally blank training fields.

metadata.title: Code of conduct and equal opportunity policy
metadata.text:
# Code of conduct and equal opportunity policy

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Code of conduct and equal opportunity policy
metadata.text:
## 1. Equal opportunity and accommodations
Make hiring, assignment, compensation, promotion, training, and separation decisions using legitimate job-related criteria. GridAxon prohibits discrimination based on protected characteristics listed in HR-001 and any other protected status under applicable law. Company policy may protect more broadly than a particular statute's coverage. Statutory coverage and eligibility must be evaluated separately; the fictional 18-person headcount does not make every employment statute applicable.
Employees and applicants may request reasonable disability, pregnancy-related, or religious accommodations through People Operations or an uninvolved manager. Engage promptly in an individualized interactive process and seek counsel where needed. Provide legally required lactation breaks and an appropriate private space other than a bathroom; use HR-009 for timekeeping. Do not require medical details to be shared with coworkers.

metadata.title: Code of conduct and equal opportunity policy
metadata.text:
## 2. Professional and technical integrity
Do not falsify study results, alter engineering assumptions to satisfy a client without disclosure, misrepresent qualifications, or sign/seal work without required authority. Escalate material study errors, unsafe field conditions, bribery requests, and conflicts of interest. Client deadlines never justify bypassing safety controls or fabricating results. Employees may stop unsafe work and promptly alert the project lead without retaliation.
Disclose outside consulting, financial interests, or family relationships that could influence assignments or purchasing. Do not accept cash gifts. Noncash business gifts above $50 require written manager approval and conflict review; client procurement rules may prohibit gifts of any value. Maintain accurate time, expense, and project records.

metadata.title: Code of conduct and equal opportunity policy
metadata.text:
## 3. Reporting and response
Report concerns to People Operations, the CEO, or the independent Board contact; bypass anyone involved. Harassment complaints follow HR-001. Security incidents follow HR-013 and HR-014. Protected external reporting needs no approval. Apply corrective action consistently after fair review. This policy does not prohibit lawful discussion of pay or working conditions.

metadata.title: PTO, holidays, sick time and protected leave
metadata.text:
# PTO, holidays, sick time and protected leave

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: PTO, holidays, sick time and protected leave
metadata.text:
## 1. PTO eligibility, accrual, and requests
Regular full-time employees scheduled for at least 30 hours per week accrue 120 PTO hours per calendar year, at 120/26 hours per biweekly pay period, starting on the hire date. Payroll retains full precision and displays balances to two decimals. Midyear hires earn only for eligible pay periods; no annual front-loading.

metadata.title: PTO, holidays, sick time and protected leave
metadata.text:
Part-time, temporary employees, and contractors receive no discretionary PTO under this sample, without limiting legal leave rights.
Request planned PTO at least 10 business days in advance. For illness or emergencies notify the manager as soon as practicable; the advance-request rule does not apply. PTO may be used for vacation, personal needs, or illness. There is no separate discretionary sick bank. Up to 40 unused hours carry into the next year; excess is forfeited at year-end only as legally permitted. Total balance cap is 160 hours; accrual pauses at the cap and resumes below it without retroactive credits. No negative balances without People Operations approval. Legally protected leave and accommodations are evaluated separately from PTO approval.

metadata.title: PTO, holidays, sick time and protected leave
metadata.text:
## 2. Holidays
Full-time eligible employees receive eight paid company holidays: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, the following Friday, Christmas Eve, and Christmas Day. Saturday holidays are observed on the preceding Friday; Sunday holidays on the following Monday. Payroll resolves overlaps prospectively without reducing the eight-day entitlement. Holiday pay and PTO are not hours actually worked for overtime calculations. Do not assume holiday work earns a premium; HR-009 governs statutory overtime.

metadata.title: PTO, holidays, sick time and protected leave
metadata.section_title: 3. Jury, military, voting, and other protected leave
metadata.text:
## 3. Jury, military, voting, and other protected leave
Notify People Operations of a jury summons promptly. GridAxon voluntarily pays up to three scheduled workdays of jury service per calendar year; additional time is unpaid for non-exempt employees unless another law or agreement applies. Do not require PTO use. Exempt salary deductions must follow salary-basis rules, including protection for a week in which work is performed; payroll reviews any jury-fee offset.

metadata.title: PTO, holidays, sick time and protected leave
metadata.section_title: 3. Jury, military, voting, and other protected leave
metadata.text:
Provide military leave, reemployment, benefits, and nondiscrimination protections under USERRA and applicable law. Give notice when legally required and practicable; do not apply an absolute advance-approval requirement or assume all military leave is paid. HR reviews benefit continuation and reinstatement individually.
For Texas voting leave, provide the necessary protected time and pay for overlap with normal work hours when the employee lacks two consecutive hours outside working hours while polls are open, consistent with applicable law and TWC guidance.

metadata.title: PTO, holidays, sick time and protected leave
metadata.section_title: 3. Jury, military, voting, and other protected leave
metadata.text:
Coordinate scheduling without denying voting rights. Do not charge protected voting time to PTO.
Texas does not generally require private employers to provide vacation or ordinary paid sick leave; these discretionary benefits are GridAxon choices. Other laws, contracts, jurisdictions, or individual protections may apply. Review FMLA employer coverage and employee eligibility separately; 18 employees does not create an automatic federal FMLA entitlement, and absence of FMLA coverage does not eliminate accommodation or other leave duties.

metadata.title: PTO, holidays, sick time and protected leave
metadata.text:
## 4. Separation and exceptions
GridAxon's fictional written policy pays accrued unused PTO at the employee's base rate on separation, subject to lawful calculation and applicable final-pay deadlines in HR-016. Holidays and future unearned accruals are not cashed out. Notify People Operations of calculation errors. HR-012 contains a separate field-assignment illness travel exception; that reimbursement exception does not add PTO or a sick bank.

metadata.title: Wage, hour, classification and timekeeping policy
metadata.text:
# Wage, hour, classification and timekeeping policy

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Wage, hour, classification and timekeeping policy
metadata.text:
## 1. Classification and pay
People Operations documents actual duties, pay method, applicable exemption tests, and work jurisdiction before approving exempt status. A salary, engineering title, degree, or employee preference alone does not establish an exemption. Reassess when duties or location change. Non-exempt employees receive at least applicable minimum wage and overtime at 1.5 times the regular rate for hours actually worked beyond 40 in the fixed workweek, Monday 12:00 a.m. through Sunday 11:59 p.m. Central Time. The regular rate may include compensation beyond base hourly pay; payroll checks bonuses and other includable amounts. No averaging across weeks or private-sector substitution of future time off for required overtime.

metadata.title: Wage, hour, classification and timekeeping policy
metadata.text:
## 2. Timekeeping and overtime
Non-exempt employees record all work daily, including remote email, required training, work calls, and compensable travel. Submit records each Friday and correct errors promptly. Never work off the clock. Managers may require advance overtime approval, but all overtime actually worked must be reported and paid even if unauthorized. Any policy discipline is separate from payment. Salaried non-exempt employees also record hours. Exempt staff record project time and leave without authorizing improper salary deductions.

metadata.title: Wage, hour, classification and timekeeping policy
metadata.text:
## 3. Meals, breaks, and travel
Company practice permits two paid 10-minute rest breaks and one unpaid 30-minute meal period for a typical eight-hour day, coordinated with work. Record the meal as unpaid only when fully relieved of duties; interrupted working meals are compensable. Rest breaks are not unpaid. These are company provisions, not a statement that Texas generally mandates adult meal/rest breaks.

metadata.title: Wage, hour, classification and timekeeping policy
metadata.text:
Additional lactation, accommodation, or safety breaks may be legally required.
Ordinary commuting is generally excluded, while job-site-to-job-site travel during the workday is generally paid. Overnight travel and driving/passenger time require fact-specific payroll review. Do not use mileage reimbursement as a substitute for paying compensable travel time. Report payroll concerns to People Operations without retaliation; escalate salary deductions for prompt review and reimbursement when improper. See HR-012 for expenses and HR-016 for final pay.

metadata.title: Independent contractor classification process
metadata.text:
# Independent contractor classification process

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Independent contractor classification process
metadata.text:
## 1. Intake before engagement
The sponsor submits a written scope, deliverables, expected duration, proposed rate, work location, equipment arrangements, supervision expectations, ability to serve other clients, and substitution/subcontracting terms. Finance verifies business identity and tax documentation through a restricted system; do not put tax IDs in the policy index. A contract label, invoice, LLC, or Form 1099 alone does not make a worker an independent contractor.

metadata.title: Independent contractor classification process
metadata.text:
## 2. Review and decision
People Operations and counsel assess the actual relationship under each applicable regime: federal wage law, IRS tax rules, Texas unemployment law, and other relevant laws. Review control, economic independence, investment, profit/loss opportunity, permanence, integration, and relevant skill/initiative without treating one generic checklist as conclusive for every statute. Classification standards and enforcement positions can change; document the current authority and date rather than relying on a frozen test in this sample.
Ongoing full-time core engineering work directed like employee work is a red flag. If classification is uncertain, pause the contractor engagement and resolve with counsel; consider employment or another lawful arrangement. Procurement cannot override the decision based on budget. Record rationale and approvals, not just a numeric score.

metadata.title: Independent contractor classification process
metadata.text:
## 3. Contracting and monitoring
After approval, execute a services agreement covering scope, acceptance, fees, expenses, confidentiality, explicit IP assignment where needed, security, and termination. Employee IP terms do not automatically transfer contractor work; obtain a contractor-specific assignment and rights review. Give only necessary system access. Review classification at renewal, at least every six months, and whenever actual duties or control changes. If misclassification is suspected, preserve records, obtain legal review, and address pay, taxes, and benefits as applicable without retaliation. Contractors do not receive employee PTO or options automatically; any eligible equity requires separate approval.

metadata.title: Remote and hybrid work policy
metadata.text:
# Remote and hybrid work policy

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Remote and hybrid work policy
metadata.text:
## 1. Eligibility and location
Texas employees may request hybrid or fully remote work with written manager and People Operations approval. Record the approved primary work address, schedule, equipment, and client restrictions. Default collaboration hours are 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Central Time on scheduled workdays, excluding approved leave and breaks; these are availability expectations, not the entire paid workday. Remote work does not change wage classification or the requirement to record all work.
Working from another US state or country requires People Operations and security approval before the location change, including temporary arrangements. Review payroll, tax, immigration, employment-law, client, and data-access constraints. No automatic permission to work internationally is created by a remote designation.

metadata.title: Remote and hybrid work policy
metadata.text:
## 2. Workspace and safety
Maintain a reasonably safe workspace and report work-related injury promptly. Use company devices, MFA, secure connectivity, and screen privacy under HR-013. Do not use shared family accounts or leave client studies accessible to others. Report connectivity issues to the manager and IT; non-exempt employees record all work actually performed. Disability and other accommodation requests follow an individualized process under HR-007 rather than discretionary remote-work approval alone.

metadata.title: Remote and hybrid work policy
metadata.text:
## 3. Costs and changes
HR-012 governs approved equipment and the $50 monthly home-internet reimbursement. This policy itself provides no separate home-office stipend. Changes or withdrawal of remote approval require reasonable notice where practicable and compliance with accommodations, signed agreements, and law. Company approval does not authorize uncompensated overtime or access to confidential data from unapproved jurisdictions.

metadata.title: Business travel and expense reimbursement policy
metadata.text:
# Business travel and expense reimbursement policy

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Business travel and expense reimbursement policy
metadata.text:
## 1. Approval and documentation
Submit business expenses within 30 calendar days with itemized receipts, date, business purpose, project code, and approval. A missing receipt may be supported by a signed explanation and Finance review. Late claims require Finance review rather than automatic denial of legally required reimbursement. Get advance manager approval for overnight travel and purchases above $250; purchases above $1,000 additionally require Finance approval. Do not split a purchase to evade limits.

metadata.title: Business travel and expense reimbursement policy
metadata.text:
## 2. Sample limits
Reimburse reasonable actual business meals up to $60 per traveler per travel day, including tax and tip. This is a cap on receipted expenses, not an automatic per diem. Alcohol is excluded. Lodging target is $180 per night before tax; higher local rates require manager approval. Use economy airfare unless a documented exception is approved. Mileage uses the IRS business rate applicable on the travel date, verified by Finance; no fixed mileage rate is encoded here.

metadata.title: Business travel and expense reimbursement policy
metadata.text:
No double claim for mileage and the same fuel cost.
Approved remote employees may claim actual home-internet cost up to $50 monthly with a bill and business-use attestation. No reimbursement for ordinary home meals, routine commuting, or personal entertainment under the discretionary policy. Legally required reimbursement and wage protections take priority over discretionary limits. Contractors follow their services agreements rather than this employee policy unless expressly incorporated.

metadata.title: Business travel and expense reimbursement policy
metadata.text:
## 3. Field-assignment illness exception
If an employee becomes ill during an approved overnight client field assignment, reasonable additional lodging and necessary transport may be reimbursed with People Operations and Finance approval, even when above ordinary limits. Notify the project lead as soon as practicable; do not delay urgent medical care to seek approval. This exception covers travel disruption, not medical insurance benefits. Illness time away from work follows HR-008 and any protected leave; reimbursement does not create extra PTO. Submit supporting receipts without unnecessary medical detail.

metadata.title: Business travel and expense reimbursement policy
metadata.text:
## 4. Payment and escalation
Finance targets reimbursement within two biweekly payroll cycles after a complete approved claim, through the approved expense process. This internal target does not extend legal payment deadlines. Escalate expenses that could reduce pay below applicable minimum wage or overtime obligations. Managers cannot promise tax treatment; Finance handles substantiation and taxable payments as required.

metadata.title: IT security and acceptable use policy
metadata.text:
# IT security and acceptable use policy

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: IT security and acceptable use policy
metadata.text:
## 1. Access and devices
Use managed company devices, individual accounts, MFA, approved password management, encryption, and timely security updates. Apply least-privilege access and project separation. Personal devices require written IT approval and agreed controls before accessing company data. Do not share passwords, disable controls, or install unauthorized tools. Limited personal use is permitted if lawful, safe, and not disruptive; it does not authorize handling others' private data.

metadata.title: IT security and acceptable use policy
metadata.text:
## 2. Client models, AI, and software
Store client network models, study cases, code, and reports only in approved repositories. Do not upload confidential, client, employee, export-controlled, or personal information into public AI assistants, public code repositories, or unapproved SaaS tools. An approved AI tool still requires data-owner permission and a permitted purpose. Synthetic learning documents may be used for the RAG lab; actual executed agreements, complaint files, and SSNs must be excluded. Review generated engineering outputs before relying on them. Software, model licenses, and client agreements may impose restrictions beyond this policy.

metadata.title: IT security and acceptable use policy
metadata.text:
## 3. Incidents, monitoring, and return
Report suspected phishing, lost devices, unauthorized access, or accidental disclosure to IT and People Operations immediately, targeting within one hour after discovery. Use an alternate communication route if the account is compromised. Preserve evidence; do not delete logs or notify clients independently. This internal target is separate from statutory breach notices in HR-014. Monitoring is limited to authorized business, security, and compliance purposes with applicable notice and legal review; no unlimited inspection of personal accounts is authorized.
At separation IT follows HR-016 to revoke access and preserve records. Remote wiping of personal devices requires approved scope and legal review to protect personal data. Nothing prevents protected agency reports or lawful discussion of employment conditions.

metadata.title: Employee privacy, SSN protection and incident response
metadata.text:
# Employee privacy, SSN protection and incident response

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Employee privacy, SSN protection and incident response
metadata.text:
## 1. Collection and access
Collect employee information only for documented employment, payroll, benefits, security, and legal purposes. Restrict payroll and identity records to authorized People Operations, Finance, and necessary service providers. Maintain medical/accommodation records separately with heightened access controls. Inform employees of relevant collection, use, sharing, retention, and access channels. Do not imply that all consumer-privacy rights automatically apply to employment data.

metadata.title: Employee privacy, SSN protection and incident response
metadata.text: Collect SSNs only through approved secure workflows when needed; never use an SSN as a badge, general login, or public identifier. Mask displays, encrypt storage and transmission, prohibit ordinary email or chat transmission, and securely destroy records under an approved retention schedule after holds expire. No real SSNs or realistic SSN placeholders belong in the RAG dataset. Requests for personnel-record corrections go to People Operations; verify identity before disclosure.

metadata.title: Employee privacy, SSN protection and incident response
metadata.text:
## 2. Incident escalation and assessment
Employees follow HR-013 immediately. IT contains exposure and preserves evidence; People Operations coordinates employee support; counsel determines whether a legally defined breach occurred, affected jurisdictions, notice triggers, contractual obligations, and any lawful delay. Discovery, determination, resident counts, decisions, and notices must be timestamped. An incident involving fewer than 250 Texans can still require individual notice; that count is not a blanket exemption.

metadata.title: Employee privacy, SSN protection and incident response
metadata.text:
## 3. Texas notice framework
Under Texas Business and Commerce Code 521.053, applicable individual notification is required as quickly as possible and generally no later than 60 days after determining the breach occurred, subject to statutory provisions and authorized delays. If at least 250 Texas residents are affected, notify the Texas Attorney General as soon as practicable and no later than 30 days after determining that the breach occurred, as required by the statute. Do not wait for these outer limits when earlier notice is required. Counsel checks the current statutory text, regulator instructions, resident jurisdictions, and additional obligations before calculating deadlines or making a notification. The company's one-hour incident-report target does not replace legal notice duties.

metadata.title: Employee privacy, SSN protection and incident response
metadata.text:
## 4. Retention and retrieval boundaries
Use an approved category-based retention schedule that accounts for payroll, personnel, I-9, medical, security, and tax duties; this sample intentionally does not invent one universal retention period. Legal holds suspend destruction. The policy assistant may index this policy text but must not index individual personnel files, identity documents, signed agreements, medical records, or investigations without a separately authorized access-controlled design.

# Illustrative equity plan, grant notice and option terms

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Illustrative equity plan, grant notice and option terms
metadata.text:
## 1. Plan status and assumptions
This is an educational term sheet and mock grant packet, not an adopted securities plan or actual issuance. Solely for this scenario, assume GridAxon is a privately held corporation authorized to issue common stock. Actual entity type, charter, capitalization, board and stockholder approvals, securities exemptions, valuation, tax treatment, and plan administration must be confirmed by corporate and tax counsel before use. A domain name does not establish corporate form. No authorized share pool or employee ownership percentage is supplied by this dataset.

metadata.title: Illustrative equity plan, grant notice and option terms
metadata.text:
## 2. Illustrative plan rules
The Board or a properly authorized committee administers awards subject to the final plan. Eligible employees and any permitted service providers require individual approval; contractors cannot receive incentive stock options as employees. An offer-letter reference is not a grant. The final plan must define the reserve, adjustment provisions, award types, eligibility, transfer restrictions, exercise procedures, tax withholding, treatment of leave, death, disability, termination for cause, transactions, and amendment authority. Unresolved terms require counsel, not inferred defaults.

metadata.title: Illustrative equity plan, grant notice and option terms
metadata.text:
## 3. Mock grant notice
Participant: [employee]. Award: 4,800 nonqualified stock options. Grant date: [Board-approved date]. Exercise price: [approved per-share amount supported by valuation and tax review]. Vesting commencement: [date]. No real grant is effective while fields or approvals are missing.
Illustrative vesting is four years with a one-year cliff: 1,200 options vest at the first anniversary and 100 monthly on each of the next 36 monthly anniversaries, subject to continuous service and final terms.

metadata.title: Illustrative equity plan, grant notice and option terms
metadata.text: No automatic acceleration is included. Unvested options ordinarily cease vesting and are forfeited on service termination under the sample, subject to final plan and protected-leave review. Vested options have an illustrative 90-calendar-day post-termination exercise window, never beyond the original 10-year term, except as the final terms and applicable law provide. Death, disability, cause, and change-of-control rules are intentionally unresolved and must not be guessed.

metadata.title: Illustrative equity plan, grant notice and option terms
metadata.text:
## 4. Exercise and acknowledgment
Exercise requires timely notice, payment, withholding arrangements, and compliance with final plan restrictions and law. Private-company shares may be illiquid and lose all value. No valuation, future funding, liquidity, percentage ownership, or tax benefit is promised. Counsel reviews Rule 701 or another applicable exemption and required disclosures; HR does not provide individual tax advice.
Participant signature: __________________ Date: __________
Company authorized signature: __________________ Date: __________
Board approval reference: __________ Valuation reference: __________
This mock packet contains no issued shares, signed grant, or operative plan.

metadata.title: Termination and offboarding checklist
metadata.text:
# Termination and offboarding checklist

> FICTIONAL TRAINING SAMPLE. Not an adopted policy or executed agreement. All company facts and benefits are invented. Requires qualified legal review before operational use.

metadata.title: Termination and offboarding checklist
metadata.section_title: 1. Before separation — People Operations and counsel
metadata.text:
## 1. Before separation — People Operations and counsel
- Confirm decision authority, reason, actual separation date, jurisdiction, and voluntary/involuntary classification; assess discrimination, retaliation, protected leave, accommodation, and contract issues.
- Preserve legal holds and relevant evidence before deleting accounts. Review HR-002 agreements, HR-004 IP, any executed covenant, HR-008 PTO, and actual equity documents under HR-015.
- Prepare final wage and benefit calculations and a respectful communication plan. Two weeks' resignation notice is requested as a courtesy, not required to preserve earned wages or the sample accrued-PTO payout.

metadata.title: Termination and offboarding checklist
metadata.section_title: 2. Separation meeting — manager and People Operations
metadata.text:
## 2. Separation meeting — manager and People Operations
- Explain the effective date, final-pay process, benefit contacts, expense submission, and property return. Do not promise severance or a release without separately reviewed documents.
- Remind the employee of lawful continuing confidentiality obligations and protected reporting rights. Do not represent the unsigned HR-005 sample as binding.
- Review the actual option grant, vested amount, exercise deadline, and administrator contact; HR-015 sample dates are not substitutes for executed terms.

metadata.title: Termination and offboarding checklist
metadata.section_title: 3. Access, assets, and knowledge — IT and project lead
metadata.text:
## 3. Access, assets, and knowledge — IT and project lead
- Coordinate access removal with the effective separation and risk assessment; promptly disable SSO, VPN, client portals, keys, tokens, cloud access, and remote sessions when authorized.
- Recover company devices, badges, and client media; provide a return method for remote staff. Rotate shared secrets and transfer authorized project ownership. Preserve required records and legal holds; do not erase evidence.
- Permit retrieval of approved personal material without exposing client data. Confirm contractor and client access separately. Do not withhold final wages merely because property is missing; deductions require an independent lawful basis and any required authorization.

metadata.title: Termination and offboarding checklist
metadata.section_title: 4. Final pay and benefits — Finance and People Operations
metadata.text:
## 4. Final pay and benefits — Finance and People Operations
For Texas involuntary separation, pay final wages within six calendar days of discharge. For voluntary resignation, pay on the next regular payday, subject to applicable law and any more protective requirement. Include earned wages and accrued unused PTO promised by HR-008; calculate other compensation under its governing terms and law. Do not assume a Friday payroll cycle extends an earlier statutory deadline.
Process reimbursable business expenses under HR-012 and applicable law. Determine coverage and eligibility for federal COBRA, Texas continuation, and other notices from the actual employer, plan, and headcount rules; the fictional 18-person count does not justify a blanket statement that all continuation rights are absent. Record notice responsibilities and due dates.

metadata.title: Termination and offboarding checklist
metadata.text:
## 5. Closeout evidence
Record owner, due date, completion timestamp, and evidence for each checklist item. Offer an optional exit interview without requiring a release. Restrict separation records under HR-014. Signed certifications, releases, and employee records stay out of the shared policy corpus.
